narration: Arvo. Sunday-night invoicing for NDIS support workers, offline, on Gemma four.
on_screen_caption: Sunday-night invoicing for NDIS support workers. Offline. Gemma 4 on your own laptop.
visual: Title slide: 'Arvo' in deep green on off-white, subtitle beneath, small Gemma 4 / Ollama line.

narration: One diary line, two traps. Tuesday, Cup Day. Jake, three till eight thirty-ish. Locked the pantry so he would stop snacking. One trap costs money. The other is a restrictive practice that reads like any other note.
visual: The diary line types itself on screen: 'Tues (Cup day!!) - Jake 3 till 8:30ish ... Locked the pantry so he would stop snacking before dinner'; 'Cup day' and 'Locked the pantry' tint red as each trap is named.

narration: Call her Mel. An independent NDIS support worker in Victoria. Nobody pays her for the admin, and a wrong item number bounces the invoice.
on_screen_caption: Mel is a composite, not a real person: built from published rate guides and NDIS Commission material. Not legal advice.
visual: Who slide: 'Independent NDIS support worker, ABN, Victoria. Admin unpaid.' and the rates table: weekday $73.58 / evening $81.07 / Saturday $103.54 / Sunday $133.50 / public holiday $163.46 per hour.

narration: Trap one. Cup Day is a Victorian public holiday. Five and a half hours at the holiday rate: eight hundred and ninety-nine dollars. On a normal Tuesday it crosses eight at night, and the whole shift bills at the evening rate. Not split.
on_screen_caption: Tue 3 Nov 2026 is Melbourne Cup Day: 5.5 h x $163.46 = $899.03 (not 5.5 h x $73.58). Pricing Schedule 2026-27 s2.4(c): "the higher of the amounts applies to the whole support".
visual: Trap 1 slide: big '5.5 h x $163.46 = $899.03', weekday $73.58 struck through, then the s2.4(c) quote in a pull-quote block.

narration: Trap two. Locking the pantry is an environmental restraint under the NDIS rules. A registered provider has five business days to notify the Commission, twenty-four hours if it caused harm. An unregistered sole trader must not use it.
on_screen_caption: Environmental restraint: NDIS (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. Registered provider: notify the NDIS Commission within 5 business days, 24 h if harm. Unregistered: must not use; raise it with the Commission. Not legal advice.
visual: Trap 2 slide: the pantry sentence in red, 'environmental restraint' label, two columns: Registered (5 business days / 24 h if harm) and Unregistered (must not use; raise with the Commission).

narration: Paste the week, press Read and price. Gemma reads it offline; the counter shows real seconds, about thirteen. Seven shifts, ten invoice lines, three flags. The red one is the pantry, quoted exactly, with its notify-by date. The PRN and bed rails: authorised, record only. Then the shifts Gemma read, the lines code priced, a Why on each, and a printable invoice per participant.
on_screen_caption: LIVE: Gemma 4 on my laptop (wait sped up)
visual: Live app: diary pasted, 'Read and price this week' pressed, counter ticks, results appear; scroll to the red 'Check before you invoice' panel (pantry highlighted, PRN and bed rails marked authorised), the shifts table, the invoice lines; one 'Why' expanded; 'Print invoice' opened.

narration: Same job from a photo of a paper diary. Drop it in and run. All seven shifts come back, read straight from the image, with a note to check them before you invoice.
on_screen_caption: LIVE: photo of a paper diary
visual: Live app: eval/fixtures/week13.png dropped onto the page, run pressed, the shifts table fills from the image.

narration: And voice. Three memos, one per shift. Gemma hears the audio directly; no separate speech model. What Gemma heard opens for checking; the shifts land in the table.
visual: Live app: three voice memos added, run pressed, about 5 s of one memo plays, the 'What Gemma heard' panel opens line by line, shifts appear in the table.

narration: The model reads, code decides. Gemma never picks a price, an item number or a deadline. Code does, from the Schedule. Let Gemma price the week itself: zero of sixteen right. A flag must quote the note, or it's dropped.
on_screen_caption: Gemma pricing the week itself: 0 of 16 weeks right (line recall 49.5%). Code pricing Gemma's shifts: 10 of 16, 95.0%.
visual: Diagram: diary / photo / voice -> Gemma 4 reads -> shifts JSON -> code decides (bands, holidays, official prices) -> invoice; second row: note -> Gemma -> flag with verbatim quote, or dropped.

narration: Held-out results. Test split: ninety-three per cent of shifts exact. Wild diaries: seventy-six per cent, where a code-only parser gets forty. Restrictive practices: e-four-b finds twenty of twenty-two restraints. Photos, ninety per cent. Voice, six of ten memos fully right.
on_screen_caption: Held out, run once on frozen code (eval-freeze-1). Test 93.3% exact (code-only 91.6%). Wild 75.9% (code-only 39.7%). Restrictive practices F1 88.9%, 20/22 restraints (keyword list 45.7%; gemma4:e2b 41.4%). Photos 90.0%. Voice 6/10.
visual: Results table slide, five rows, Arvo column in green beside baselines; the wild row and the restrictive-practice row emphasised.

narration: My guardrails overruled right answers. Seven of fourteen wrong wild shifts were my code overwriting Gemma's correct value. New rule: code overrules Gemma only when Gemma's value is impossible. After the fix, no longer held out, wild goes to ninety-five per cent.
on_screen_caption: 7 of 14 wrong wild shifts: code overwrote a correct Gemma value. Rule: code overrules the model only when its own reading is unambiguous and the model's value is impossible. After the fix (not held out): wild 94.8%, 7/8 weeks to the cent.
visual: Lesson slide: title 'My guardrails overruled right answers'; the warning line "start set to 09:00 from '9 30 till 1 30' (model said 09:30)"; before/after pair 75.9% -> 94.8%, 2/8 -> 7/8, marked 'not held out'.

narration: Why open weights? Shift notes are sensitive health information. On her own laptop, nothing leaves. Offline in a car park, zero dollars a week, on a six gigabyte laptop GPU.
on_screen_caption: Shift notes are 'sensitive information' (Privacy Act s 6). Server binds to 127.0.0.1. Offline. $0 a week. 6 GB laptop GPU, or a CPU-only GitHub Actions runner (run 38347559687).
visual: Why-open slide: four short lines (stays on the laptop / offline / $0 a week / 6 GB GPU or CPU runner) with a small screenshot of the green GitHub Actions gemma-smoke run.

narration: Who pays? Independent workers like Mel, at twelve dollars a month. The agency tools charge per user, five staff minimum.
on_screen_caption: Proposed: $12 a month or $99 a year for solo ABN workers. ShiftCare pricing: per user, "All plans start at a minimum of five staff".
visual: Who-pays slide: '$12 / month' large in green; beside it a muted crop of the ShiftCare pricing page with the five-staff minimum line.

narration: On GitHub: Otto Deviant nineteen-oh-four, slash arvo. Open code, open weights. The model reads, code decides, and nothing leaves the laptop.
